title: Keyboard-first globalization audit and remediation for cost & rollouts dashboards
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Audit and remediate accessibility and localization gaps on the Cost Overview and Rollouts dashboards with a keyboard-first approach. Deliver a developer-friendly spec, interactive Figma prototype, and a prioritized fix list for engineering. Focus areas: full keyboard/arrow navigation, predictable focus order, semantic focus rings, WCAG color-contrast adjustments for cost cards and charts, locale-aware number/date formatting, and RTL layout sanity checks. Include acceptance criteria, implementation trade-offs, and QA matrix for screen readers and keyboard-only users.
acceptance_criteria: All interactive elements on Cost Overview and Rollouts are reachable and operable via keyboard (Tab, Shift+Tab, Arrow keys where relevant)
Visual focus indicator is visible at 3x current token size and meets contrast ratio with the surrounding element
Primary text meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) and large text meets WCAG AAA (7:1) where copy is >18px in highlighted states
Numerical and currency values render according to selected locale and respect user overrides in profile
RTL switch renders dashboard grids, overflow menus, and tooltips without clipping or reflow regressions
Live rollout status updates announce changes using accessible live regions (polite) without disrupting focus
Figma prototype reviewed and signed off by PM and Eng, and dev PR includes unit/integration tests referencing QA matrix
tasks: Run automated contrast and semantic HTML audit across both dashboards (axe, pa11y) and capture failures
Map current focus order and tab stops; create keyboard flows and identify trap areas
Design updated focus tokens and fallback visual styles for high-density cost cards
Prototype arrow-key navigation patterns for the rollouts table (row/column focus) and test with VoiceOver/NVDA
Add localized number/date variants to design tokens and create examples for fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP, ar-SA
Coordinate with infra on locale header fallback and with backend on number formatting toggle (design-only if backend delayed)
Produce dev spec doc with CSS patterns, ARIA recommendations, and regression test checklist
comments: 2026-02-20 - Ava M: Initial discovery complete. Ran base axe scan; major issues concentrated on custom card controls and chart tooltips. Created keyboard flow diagrams and initial Figma file.

2026-02-25 - Liam O'C: Reviewed flows. Engineering flagged chart library as a risk — current library intercepts arrow keys. Proposal: implement a scoped key-capture shim that only activates when chart receives focus.
2026-03-01 - PM (Sophie R): Prioritize numeric localization for billing regions (EU and APAC). If backend formatting isn't available in time, implement client-side locale formatter as interim.

2026-03-04 - Accessibility review (External consultant): Recommend switching from aria-hidden on complex SVGs to exposing simplified accessible text alternatives to preserve semantics for screen readers.

2026-03-08 - Design note: Decided to use 'aria-roledescription' on rollout status badges for clearer announcements. Avoided over-reliance on role="status" to prevent unexpected screen reader verbosity.

2026-03-10 - Engineering review (PR mockup): Agreed on focus token semantics and accepted prototype for arrow-key table navigation. Engineering requests smaller batch of CSS token changes to land first to reduce churn.
design_decisions: Prefer native semantic elements (button, table, a) over role-based replacements where possible to reduce keyboard and AT surface area
Use a focused token palette with two contrast scales: ‘accent-focus’ for interactive edges and ‘surface-focus’ for container outlines to avoid visual clutter in dense grids
Implement arrow-key navigation within rollout rows but keep Tab/Shift+Tab for high-level traversal to preserve expected browser behaviour
Defer locale preference persistence until backend feature lands; implement UI-level formatter and flag for users in EU/APAC as interim
qa_matrix: Screen readers: NVDA (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS), TalkBack (Android) - smoke pass for all keyboard flows
Keyboard-only: Chromium, Firefox, Safari - tab order, shift-tab, arrow nav, escape to close modals
Localization: verify number/currency/date formatting for fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP, ar-SA and fallback to en-US
RTL: mirror layout, ensure focus ring alignment and no clipping of dropdowns/tooltips
Contrast: run automated regressed tests plus manual color pair checks in dark/light themes
notes_for_engineering: Provide a lightweight key-capture shim for the chart component that respects focus and prevents global keyboard traps
Avoid setting tabindex>0 in new components; use tabindex=0 and DOM ordering for predictable tab sequence
Expose a small set of semantic data attributes (data-key-order) for complex composed controls to help with QA automation
Include unit tests for client-side locale formatter (if used) and integration tests that assert formatted strings for each region
